chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Can one marry a Magian woman?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but if there was such a slave girl for him'.

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Can a Muslim man marry a free Magian woman according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific juristic distinction between free and enslaved Magian women, reflecting the Shia view that the permissibility of marrying 'People of the Book' extends to their female slaves under certain conditions. It highlights the nuance in Usuli jurisprudence where the status of the woman (free vs. slave) dictates the validity of the marriage contract with a Muslim man.
